# Kit Registry: chuang-platform-kit

**Generated by `python scripts/build-kit-registry.py` from the docstrings: do not edit by hand; edit the
docstring and regenerate.** `tests/test-kit-registry.py` fails when this file is stale or a public name has no
docstring.

**Kit first:** before writing anything a second project could use (a retry, a REST client, a webhook's
check, a once-only claim, a sender), read this file. If the kit has it, import it; if it is close, change the
kit (a kit commit, a tag, the pin bump in each host). A host's own registry lists only its own code.

The `chuang_sdlc.` sections are chuang-sdlc, the ticket tools: a distribution of its own in `sdlc/`, pinned
only where they run (its own tags, `sdlc-v<version>`). The `chuang_alerts.` sections are chuang-alerts, a
project's alerting: a distribution of its own in `alerts/` (its own tags, `alerts-v<version>`). The
`chuang_app_pipeline.` sections are chuang-app-pipeline, an Expo app's pipeline: a distribution of its own in
`app-pipeline/` (its own tags, `app-v<version>`), standard library only.

## `cache`: In-process answers kept for a few seconds, a per-caller throttle, and a once-a-window gate: the rea…

|---|---|
| `get(key, clock=)` | The value kept under `key`, or None when there is none or it is stale. |
| `put(key, value, ttl, clock=)` | Keep `value` under `key` for `ttl` seconds; the value back, so `cache.get(k) or cache.put(k, load(), 30)` reads as one line. |
| `cached(key, ttl, load, clock=)` | The kept value under `key`, or `load()` kept for `ttl` seconds. A falsy answer (an empty list) is kept too, which `get() or put()` would re-load. |
| `clear(prefix=)` | Drop every kept answer (or those whose key starts with `prefix`): a write happened, so the next read is fresh. |
| `throttle(key, limit, window, clock=)` | None when this call is within `limit` calls per `window` seconds for `key`, else the whole seconds to wait (at least 1) before the next. Count only the calls the cache could not answer, and give each caller (a session, a device, a job) its own key: on 10/6/26… |
| `once(key, window, clock=)` | True the first time `key` is asked in each `window` seconds, False until then: a warning said once a minute however often it applies. |
| `reset()` | Forget everything (the tests' fresh start). |

## `config`: A versioned configuration document, read at runtime from one source, cached, with a change signal.

| Name | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `class Document` | One read of the configuration: its `version` (any string that changes when the content does: an updated-at stamp, a hash, a counter), its `data` (a mapping) and when it was read. |
| `lookup(data, key, default=)` | The value at a dotted `key` path ('booking.target_time') in nested mappings, else `default`; a flat key with a dot in it is tried first, so either spelling works. |
| `class Config` | A cached, versioned configuration document with a change signal (module docstring). |
| `Config.version()` | The current document's version, '' before one has been read. |
| `Config.mark_dirty()` | A change signal: the next read fetches again, whatever the ttl says. |
| `Config.on_change(callback)` | Call `callback(old_version, new_version)` whenever a new document is taken. |
| `Config.refresh(force=)` | Read the source if it is time (ttl passed, dirty, or `force`): True when a new document was taken, False when unchanged, skipped or unreachable (then `stale` says so). |
| `Config.get(key, default=)` | The value for `key` (a dotted path): the document's, else the fallback's (before any document has been read), else the code's default, else `default`; KeyError when none has it. A fallback value that disagrees with the document is a WARNING, once per key. |
| `Config.typed(key, kind, default=)` | `get(key)` coerced to `kind` (bool reads 'true'/'1'/'yes' from a string); a value that cannot be coerced answers `default` (or raises ValueError without one). |
| `Config.snapshot()` | Every key as the reads would answer it: the defaults under the document (or the fallback). |
| `etag(version)` | The ETag for a document version (quoted, as the header wants it). |
| `unchanged(if_none_match, version)` | True when a request's If-None-Match names the current version (the 304 case). |
| `provider(config, name=)` | An OpenFeature provider over a Config: every flag read is `config.get(key)`, typed, with the document's version as the variant. Needs the `config` extra (openfeature-sdk). |

## `firestore`: Firestore over REST with the standard library: documents, commits, queries, create-only claims and…

| Name | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `class Unreachable` | Firestore could not be read or written: no token, a network error, a refusal, a 5xx. The message names the HTTP status and Firestore's status word, or the exception's kind; never a token. |
| `class Conflict` | A commit's precondition did not hold (the document exists for a create-only write, or it changed since the read an update named): Firestore's ALREADY_EXISTS, FAILED_PRECONDITION or ABORTED. |
| `encode(value)` | One Python value as a Firestore REST value, decode's inverse: None, bool, int, float, str, bytes, a datetime (a timestampValue in UTC; a naive one is read as UTC), lists or tuples and dicts of them; anything else as its str(). |
| `decode(value)` | One Firestore REST value as plain Python: integers and doubles as numbers, arrays and maps in kind, null as None, bytes as bytes, a timestamp, a reference or a geo point as Firestore wrote it (text, or a {latitude, longitude} dict). None for anything that is… |

## `lazy_import`: A module imported on first use, not at import time.

| Name | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `lazy(name)` | A stand-in for module `name` that imports it on its first attribute read. |
| `lazy_attr(module, attr)` | A stand-in for `from module import attr` that imports `module` on its first call or attribute read. |
| `importable(*names)` | True when every module in `names` is installed, without importing any of them (only their parent packages). |
| `require(*names)` | Raise ImportError unless every module in `names` is installed (see importable()): the fail-fast an eager import gave. |

Neon's paid plans have spending notifications but no hard cap, so the compute ceiling… |

## `outbox`: The transactional outbox: an event written with its record, published after the commit, swept when…

| Name | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `emit(s, model, envelope, ordering_key=, key=, **columns)` | One event in `s`'s transaction: its `model` row, for `dispatch` after the commit. The envelope's id, which the row keeps as its own; the ids are remembered in `s.info[key]` in emit order. |
| `drop(s, model, key=)` | Take back the events `s` emitted and has not dispatched (the caller commits): its write was undone. |
| `send_rows(s, rows, publish, topic, attributes, failure, state, stuck=, log=, label=)` | Publish each row in order, stamp the sent ones' `published_at` and count a refused one's `attempts` (an ERROR line once it reaches `stuck`), then commit. (sent, failed). |
| `dispatch(s, model, publish, topic, attributes, failure, state, key=, sweep_after_s=, limit=, stuck=, log=, label=)` | After the commit: publish the events `s` emitted, in the order it emitted them, and stamp them; then, when the state asks (a failure or a start left rows behind) and none failed now, sweep. {sent, failed, swept}. Never raises. |
| `sweep(s, model, publish, topic, attributes, failure, state, now=, after_s=, limit=, stuck=, log=, label=)` | Publish every unstamped row older than `after_s`, oldest first, at most `limit`. {sent, failed, left}: `left` the unstamped rows still there after it. The state keeps asking while any are left, or the limit was reached, or one failed (a sweep within `after_s`… |
| `stage(envelope, ordering_key=, attributes=)` | One event for the Firestore outbox: {id, envelope, ordering_key, attributes}, for `fs_writes` in the record's own commit and `publish_staged` after the answer. |
| `fs_writes(collection, staged, now, keep_days=)` | The Firestore writes that keep `staged` events pending, for the record's own commit: each its `<collection>/<id>` document, created only (a second write of one id is refused with its commit), with the TTL field `keep_days` ahead. |
| `publish_staged(staged, publish, store, topic, failure, state, after_s=, limit=, log=, label=)` | After the answer: publish the events a record's commit kept (`stage`, `fs_writes`) and mark them; then, when the state asks and none failed now, sweep. {sent, failed, swept}. Never raises. |
| `sweep_fs(store, publish, topic, failure, state, now=, after_s=, limit=, scan=, log=, label=)` | Publish every pending document older than `after_s`, oldest first, at most `limit` (reading at most `scan`). {sent, failed, left}, `left` the pending ones it did not send (too young, or past the limit). |

| `drop(key)` | Forget `key` in this scope: the request just wrote to what it read. |
| `mark(step)` | End a step on this scope's timer; nothing outside a labelled scope. |
